Earlier this year, rumors were swirling that iOS 26.4 would introduce a revamped Health app. The project was later delayed, and with iOS 27 now out, it still hasn't materialized.

With the new Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 debuting next month, it's worth asking: will these new features arrive alongside the new hardware?

Precedent

First, it's worth looking back at why these features might well appear in September. You might think, "Shouldn't all software be announced in June?" — but there's actually precedent for this.

watchOS 9's Low Power Mode, watchOS 11's sleep apnea detection, and watchOS 26's hypertension notifications all launched in September, despite not requiring the latest hardware to function.

So based on the above, there's a strong chance Apple will wait until September to unveil its latest Health app upgrade — even if the features don't necessarily need new Apple Watch hardware to work.

Still Time

Before WWDC27, Bloomberg's Mark Gurman warned that the new Health app upgrade, codenamed Project Mulberry, might not appear during the WWDC keynote. As it turned out, he was right:

Does this mean Project Mulberry will definitely appear at the September keynote? Not necessarily. That said, given the history of features launching in September, and given that we already knew its rollout might come after WWDC, a September debut seems quite likely — even if the actual release might not come until iOS 27.1 in October.

Feature Recap

Rumors about this suite of features have gone back and forth, since there are many variables involved. You may have heard that one piece of it was a standalone Health+ service with doctor-recorded videos. However, that plan has reportedly been scaled back, with the features instead being folded into the existing Health app experience.

Two things are fairly clear, though: an AI health coach will be added, offering health advice based on your Health app data, and the ability to use the camera to give you real-time guidance on fitness and other health-related tasks. Another key part of this upgrade is a fresh new design for the Health app, making your data easier to see at a glance.

Beyond that, we'll have to wait and see. Personally, I'm quite looking forward to having a better way to organize and understand my Apple Health data.
